title: Mini-SKU anchoring roughpad
content:
Goal: sketch a tiny, low-friction SKU (mini) that captures value for latency-sensitive light usage (chat snippets / single-turn completions) while giving a clean path to commit/upgrade.

Constraints / product fundamentals (quick):
- target persona: product engineer adding a chat assistant for a consumer-ish app (low config). Wants cheap baseline, upgradeable to reserved for scale.
- typical session: 1–5 turns, 50–400 tokens per turn, lots of short requests (button tap autocomplete, small clarifying Qs).
- latency SLO matters: customers value ~<200ms p50 for small requests (per-route).

Back-of-the-envelope unit math (aim to be conservative):
1) Infra cost baseline (hosted):
- baseline GPU-hour blended infra cost (amortized + infra + ops): $6/hr (conservative for shared pool).
- throughput assumption for tiny requests: 600 small requests/min per GPU when batching efficiently (microbatching + KV cache saving).
- so 1 GPU handles ~36k requests/hr. Cost per request = $6 / 36k = $0.0001667 (~0.00017).
- if average small request is 150 tokens generated -> token cost (infra) = 0.00017 / 150 = 1.13e-6 $/token (infra only).

2) Add model licensing / downstream costs:
- assume open model with no per-token license cost for hosted catalog (but add S3/storage, egress, monitoring): +20% margin -> blended request cost ~ $0.0002.

3) Expected margin and price anchor:
- we want 60–70% gross margin on mini SKU to leave room for support/discounts.
- target price per small request = $0.0006 (=> gross margin ~67% if cost $0.0002).
- translate to token price: $0.0006 / 150 = $0.000004 per token (= $0.004 per 1k tokens).

4) Credit/pack translation (UX):
- simplest: expose price as "mini-credits" where 1 credit = 1 small request. Bundle: 10k credits = $6.
- alternate: charge per-token at $0.004/1k tokens (rounded nicely to $0.004).

Tier ideas (sketches):
A) Pay-as-you-go mini: $0.004 per 1k tokens, no commit. For fast adoption; aimed at hobbyists.
B) Mini-subscribe (monthly): $6/mo for 10k credits (equiv to $0.0006/request), includes soft SLO priority (lower latency queue). Users auto-upgraded to burst capacity when above 80% usage.
C) Commitment ladder: commit $X/month -> get mini-rate + 20% additional reserved capacity for spikes (helps smoothing).
D) Hybrid session-bundle: sell "20 session pack" for $1.50 (assumes 200 tokens/turn * 5 turns avg). Good for onboarding/placements.

Latency premium / SLO weight:
- propose pricing multiply factor for "ultra" tier where requests routed to low-latency pool (pre-warmed instances): +50% price. So mini $0.0006/request -> mini-ultra $0.0009/request.
- can expose as "priority credits" for customers who care about UX.

Breakpoints and churn considerations:
- conversion from free/trial: give 500 free mini-credits (good for ~500 small interactions).
- typical activation pattern: 1) try free -> 2) buy 10k credits monthly -> eventually commit to reserved when sustained high qps. We want pricing to make reserved attractive at ~>1M tokens/month.

Sensitivity table (rough):
- If actual throughput per GPU is only 250 requests/min (bad path), cost per request ~= $0.0004 -> our margin halves. Need to ensure reserve or auto-scale triggers to mitigate.
- If batching improvements push throughput to 1200/min -> cost/request $0.000083 -> large margin upside.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate micro-throughput numbers with serving runtime team (Tomás) — PRIC-342 assigned. Need empirical traces for 50–400 token flows.
- Decide whether credits are per-request or per-token in UI (simpler mental model vs accuracy).
- How to handle multi-turn session affinity (if we cache prefix, cost per subsequent turn much lower). Could sell "session tickets" that amortize first-turn cost across session.
- Edge-case: embeddings/semantic search calls can be tiny tokens but heavy compute; exclude from mini SKU or price separately.

Notes on packaging and UX friction: 
- Keep sign-up friction minimal: auto-convert remaining credits to payg if under/over.
- Offer a single sticky CTA: "Buy mini credits" in console with clear equivalence to X small chats.
- Provide in-console calculator: input expected turns/day -> recommended monthly pack.

Quick mental check vs competitors:
- Many APIs price 1k tokens at $0.02+ for larger models; our mini SKU at $0.004/1k tokens is positioned as bargain for short interactions and will help land product-led demos.

Next steps (practical):
- get 3 sample workloads from CS (hobby app, internal demo, gaming chat) to simulate token distribution -> run through cost model.
- ask serving-runtime for per-GPU sustained throughput numbers for small requests (5–200 tokens) (data by 2026-02-20 ideally).
- mock console microflow and copy for credit UX; run with Maya for design review.

Scratchpad math (raw):
- $6/hr GPU, 600 req/min => 36k/hr => $6/36k = 0.0001667/request
- 150 tokens avg -> 0.0001667/150 = 1.112e-6 $/token infra -> 0.000004 $/token retail target (4x markup) -> $0.004/1k tokens.

Random heuristics (notes-to-self):
- keep min-bundle price under $5 to reduce friction. $6 is borderline but aligns to 10k credits mapping. Maybe $4 for 6k credits is psychologically better.
- price psych: prefer round numbers in console (eg $5, $10). Could offer 6k credits for $4.99.

End of mini-sku roughpad.

[signature] Avery

(choppy, please treat as live draft; will iterate after we get throughput traces and customer protos)
